title: Build objects and arrays from constructor references

blocks.text: A constructor reference (`ArrayList::new`, `StringBuilder::new`) is a factory: each call of the interface's method runs the constructor and returns a **new** object. The interface decides which constructor: a `Supplier` calls the no-argument one, a `Function<String, T>` a one-argument one. An array constructor reference (`String[]::new`) is the `IntFunction` that `Stream.toArray` needs for a typed array.

items: `<C> List<C> buckets(int count, Supplier<C> factory)` returns `count` objects made by `factory`.
`<T> List<T> build(List<String> names, Function<String, T> factory)` makes one object per name, in order.
`String[] shout(List<String> words)` returns the words upper-cased, as a `String[]`.

blocks.text: The buckets are meant to be filled separately afterwards.

cases.says: It builds buckets, wrapped names and a typed array with the constructors it is given.
A constructor reference builds a new object on every call, so filling one bucket leaves the others empty.

concepts: String[]::new is the IntFunction that Stream.toArray needs to return a typed array.
A constructor reference is a factory that builds a new object each time it is called, with the interface choosing the constructor.
